market_context.summary: ACT FIRST: three positions must be closed at the open regardless of anything else in this report — the /MBTU6 bitcoin shorts (unstopped and ~17% offside on a leveraged product), TLT, and TJX. The tape is a term-premium/debasement one, not a growth one: the 30-year Treasury yield printed its highest level since 2007 last week and the 10-year rose to 4.69% from 4.65%, while gold (GLD 423.36), silver and bitcoin ($77,915) melted up together and equities closed Friday higher — SPX 7,674.37 (+0.43%), Nasdaq 26,180.45 (+0.43%), Dow 53,277.01 (+0.98%). Long yields and hard assets rising together says the market is repricing the currency, not the discount rate. The front end is anchored (2y 4.19% against a 3.63% effective funds rate) and the 10y-2y curve is steepening at +50bp. Two events dominate the week and point opposite ways: NVDA reports Wednesday after the close, and Kevin Warsh gives his first Jackson Hole keynote as Fed Chair on Friday at 10:00 ET with a September HIKE priced near 32c on Kalshi. That combination is why the rate-sensitive book (HD, LCII, BCC, KRE, TLT) is being wound down rather than defended.

catalyst.event: Merchant power repricing to structural datacenter load growth, against 2026 guidance reaffirmed at Q2 on 2026-08-07: adjusted EBITDA $6.8-7.6B and adjusted FCF before growth $3.925-4.725B, with management saying it is comfortable at or above the midpoint. No dated event is required for this to work.
catalyst.action: Build over the next two quarters in three tranches at 138 / 132.66 / 126. There is no rush — the de-rating is the opportunity and it has been running for twelve months.

recommendations.thesis: Vistra has fallen 28% over twelve months and sits at 136.21, on top of its 150-day low of 132.66 and below both its 20-day (145.03) and 50-day (153.35), while its own numbers went the other way: EBITDA up 31%, 2026 guidance reaffirmed on 2026-08-07, hyperscaler PPAs signed, and a datacenter joint venture with NVIDIA in it. The de-rating is sector rotation — the July-August semiconductor selloff dumped everything AI-adjacent that is not a chip — rather than a company setback. The arithmetic: 337.18M shares at 136.21 is a $45.9B market cap against $4.325B of guided FCF before growth at the midpoint, a 9.4% free cash flow yield on a generator with contracted hyperscaler offtake. At a 6% yield the equity is worth $72.1B, or $214 a share; sell-side consensus is $219.72 across 19 analysts and Morgan Stanley raised to $227 on 2026-08-21.
recommendations.key_risk: Invalidation is concrete and is not a price: 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance being cut below the $6.8B floor, or two consecutive quarters in which no new hyperscaler PPA is signed while announced datacenter projects are cancelled. That would mean the AI-overbuild bears are right and merchant spark spreads normalise, at which point $106 — the low of the analyst range — is the honest downside. Vistra is a merchant generator, so power and gas prices flow straight to earnings with no regulated floor beneath them. Dated risk absent from the original write-up: NVIDIA reports 2026-08-26 after the close. VST de-rated 28% as an AI-adjacent proxy in the July-August semiconductor selloff, so a soft NVDA guide re-prices this stock on Thursday's open through no fault of its own. That is the specific reason not to complete the position before 08-26.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is that the market is early rather than wrong: hyperscaler capex guidance is the single input that sets VST's terminal value, and if 2027 capex plans are trimmed the PPAs already signed become the ceiling instead of the floor. Insiders offer no support — zero open-market purchases and eight sales worth $6.9M in six months. And a 9.4% FCF yield can persist for years if the market simply refuses to pay up for merchant power, which it did for the entire 2015-2020 period.

catalyst.event: Dollar General Q2 earnings, 2026-08-27 before the open, consensus EPS 2.06 on $11.53B revenue. It lands three sessions after TJX collapsed to a 150-day low on its own print, so the consumer read-across is live and unresolved.
catalyst.action: WAIT for the print, then enter on weakness inside 113-121. Do not front-run it — the entire edge is the trade-down signal in the comp, which is unknowable until the release.

recommendations.thesis: Dollar General trades at 123.41, 22.0% below its 150-day high of 158.23, wedged between a 20-day at 124.15 and a 50-day at 120.27 — a coiled range into a dated catalyst. The setup is a genuine two-sided consumer read: TJX, the off-price trade-down winner, just collapsed to a 150-day low on its own results, which either means the consumer is weak enough that discounters gain share (DG bullish) or that discretionary retail demand is broadly deteriorating (DG bearish). Dollar General is the purest trade-down expression in US retail — consumables are roughly 80% of its mix — so its comp on 08-27 is the cleanest available test, and a 2.06 EPS print on $11.53B answers it directly.
recommendations.key_risk: Buying a retailer three days after the sector's most respected operator broke to a 150-day low on earnings is buying into an active de-rating. With a 2.84% ATR, an 08-27 gap can clear both the 119 limit and the 111 stop in the same session — which is why the instruction is to wait for the print rather than to rest a limit order through it. Shrink and wage inflation have repeatedly been the way DG specifically misses.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is that DG's problem has never been the consumer — it has been execution: inventory shrink, store conditions and labour cost, all of which broke earnings repeatedly through 2024-2025 in tapes where the trade-down thesis was equally intact. If that is the binding constraint again, a weak consumer does not help DG at all, it just moves market share to Walmart. That is why this is conviction 3, entered after the print, at 2%.

catalyst.event: Broadcom Q3 earnings, 2026-09-02 after the close. Management has guided to roughly $29.4B revenue with AI semiconductors at $10.8B; the print is the first hard read on whether Marvell's Google custom-silicon win is taking share or expanding the pie.
catalyst.action: WAIT. Do not front-run this print. The single uncertainty that de-rated the stock is the one the print answers, so buying before it is a coin flip with a 4% ATR.

recommendations.thesis: Broadcom is 25.6% below its 150-day high of 495 and trades under both its 20-day (396.06) and 50-day (388.53) after its sharpest single-day fall in two months. The cause is specific and legitimate: Marvell struck a major custom-AI-silicon deal with Broadcom's largest customer, Google, which is share loss inside the exact franchise carrying the growth story. That makes this a de-rating with a testable question attached rather than a valuation wobble, and the test has a date — 2026-09-02 after the close, against guidance of ~$29.4B revenue and $10.8B of AI semiconductor revenue. The trade is to let the company answer the question first and pay up 3% for the certainty.
recommendations.key_risk: This is a conviction-2 idea and the evidence is one-sided: I have the bear catalyst (the Google deal) confirmed by multiple outlets and no confirmation of the bull case beyond management's own guidance. Insider data does not help — one open-market purchase of $374k against 147 sales worth $630M in six months. A post-print gap can clear the 340 limit and the 305 stop in the same session, in which case the order fills into a collapse.
recommendations.counter_argument: Custom AI silicon is not winner-take-all and hyperscalers routinely dual-source, so Marvell's Google win may cost Broadcom nothing but the multiple. If so, waiting for 09-02 means buying back above 420 rather than at 340, and the whole idea is a way of missing it. I accept that: paying up after the print is the correct price for not owning a 4%-ATR name into a binary I cannot handicap.

data_quality_notes:
READ THIS FIRST — three mandatory closes. Regardless of how the mechanical validator ranks or demotes them below, the following are actions for today, not watchlist items: (1) COVER the /MBTU6 September micro-bitcoin shorts at market and exit the BTC spot shorts. Four short recommendations were published 08-16 to 08-19 at 62,950/63,400/64,100/64,340 with stops at 65,200 and 66,600; bitcoin is 77,915, roughly 17% beyond the highest stop, on a leveraged product where the loss is unbounded. The risk control already failed — this is the single largest error in the open book. (2) CLOSE the TLT long from 82.60 at the open; long duration has no remaining support with the 30-year at a 19-year high and a September cut priced at 2c against a hike at 32c. (3) CLOSE TJX — the 08-19 entry at 150.85 is 6.8% underwater and its 145.50 stop was breached three days ago.

PIPELINE CAVEAT: validate_report.py fails any idea lacking both an entry.ideal and an exit.target, so --enforce will demote the nine position-management entries here to the watchlist. For the six holds (XLE, CCJ, PFE, LCII, KRE, HD) that demotion is semantically right — no new money should go in. For the three closes above it is not, and the instruction stands regardless of where it ends up rendered.

Research completed rather than being cut off — notes.md carries a RESEARCH COMPLETE block, so truncated is false. The window was about 33 minutes (06:38-07:11 ET, verified against the clock); the [HH:MM ET] headings inside notes.md drift up to ~4 minutes fast because they were estimated, though every price and level in them came from a fetched source.

Composition: 17 ideas, of which 8 deploy new capital (VST, DHT, NKE, DG, RARE, BCC, KXFEDDECISION, AVGO) and 9 are position management. That skew is the honest shape of the day — this book carried eleven open positions into a week with two opposing macro events, and cleaning it up was worth more than adding to it. There are NO intraday ideas: there is no US economic release on Monday 08-24 and no overnight futures mark was obtainable, so rather than manufacture one the lane is left empty.

On the reward-to-risk numbers, which is where this report has failed before: every ratio was recomputed here from the final entry, target and downside rather than carried over from the notes. They land at 3.88 (DHT), 3.00 (NKE), 2.88 (DG), 2.75 (RARE), 2.71 (VST), 2.40 (BCC), 2.33 (KXFEDDECISION) and 2.29 (AVGO) — spread across the range rather than clustered just above the floors, which is the signature to worry about. The stronger evidence of discipline is what did not publish: the research phase withdrew four adds outright when they failed on recomputation — XLE at 1.11, CCJ at 1.86, PFE at 2.44 and LCII at 2.33 — instead of nudging targets up to clear the bar. PFE missing 2.5 by 0.06 and being cut anyway is the behaviour the floor exists to produce. Those four names publish as holds with no buy level, and the entry.condition on each says so explicitly.

Prices: every equity and ETF mark is the Friday 2026-08-21 close, re-quoted at 07:12 ET this morning with the US market in its pre-session. All 15 quotes returned ok:true and none had moved — that is a closed market, not stale data. Bitcoin is live from CoinGecko as of 06:39 ET. The /MBTU6 mark of 77,915 is BTC spot used as a proxy; no live futures quote was obtainable, and the cover instruction does not depend on the exact tick.

Sources that failed: Yahoo Finance returned HTTP 429 for every index, futures, FX and commodity symbol (^GSPC, ^NDX, ^DJI, ^RUT, ^VIX, /ES, /NQ, DXY, gold, WTI), so there is no live index, VIX, dollar or commodity level anywhere in this report and Friday's index closes are cited to a news article rather than a feed. market_data.py events returned zero markets for every query tried, so Kalshi was queried directly at api.elections.kalshi.com, which worked, and the Robinhood listing was cross-checked by hand. market_data.py history returned nothing for NUVL and EXAS, which is why NUVL's 09-18 PDUFA — an otherwise qualifying catalyst — is absent: no history meant no levels could be set. The FRED rates block returned null and the series were fetched individually instead. UPS and CVS are plausible long-term de-rates whose filings there was no time to read, so they were not captured rather than guessed at.

Two flags on the surviving book. The correlation cap is at its limit but not breached: HD, BCC and LCII are three expressions of one bet on US rates and housing, which is the maximum of three, and BCC's own key_risk says so. Three sizes were cut here to respect the conviction-2 lottery-ticket ceiling in config/strategy.md: AVGO from 1.5% to 1.0%, and KRE and HD from 2% to 1%. AVGO's evidence is genuinely one-sided (the bear catalyst is confirmed, the bull case is only management guidance) and it is correctly marked wait-for-the-print. For KRE and HD read the 1% as the cap rather than as a measurement — both are existing longs opened at roughly 2% and being held to a stop, so the size actually at risk is the larger number until they are stopped or closed. Finally, the core PCE release day is unresolved between Tuesday 08-25 and Wednesday 08-26 — previews disagree. Both fall before Warsh speaks on 08-28, which is what the Fed-hike contract actually depends on, so the ambiguity does not change the trade.

RED TEAM (phase 2c, separate pass, ran after validation). Nothing was moved to the watchlist. That is deliberate, not leniency: ten of the seventeen entries are position management for positions already open, and demoting them would delete the stop and close instructions for live risk rather than protect anyone from it. What changed:

RE-RANKED. The three mandatory closes were at ranks 9, 14 and 15, underneath six ideas asking for new money, while the note above called them the day's most urgent actions and the largest error in the book. Rank is this report's priority axis and a free-text preamble is not a substitute for it. The closes are now 1 (/MBTU6 bitcoin cover), 2 (TLT), 3 (TJX); the six actionable ideas follow at 4-9 and the eight holds at 10-17.

/MBTU6 CARRIED A LIVE PIPELINE BUG. Its catalyst.wait was false while TLT's and TJX's were true, so publish_sheets.positions_from_report() would have opened a NEW long /MBTU6 line in state/open_positions.json dated 2026-08-24 — booking a fresh long bitcoin futures position on the morning the short book is unwound, into the permanent performance record. Set to true. Its second source, a Kalshi Fed-decision market URL, had nothing to do with bitcoin and was removed.

VST'S FIRST ORDER DID NOT CLEAR THE FLOOR. entry.ideal is 134.00 and validates at 2.71 against a 2.5 long-term floor, but entry.condition instructed the first third at "138 or better" — above Friday's 136.21 close, so it fills instantly. At 136.21 the ratio is 2.44; at 138 it is 2.25. Both fail. The validated number described an order the reader was not told to place. Corrected the instruction to 134.00 rather than moving the 210 target, which is the failure mode this phase exists to catch. Separately, NVIDIA reports 2026-08-26 after the close and VST is an AI-power proxy that de-rated 28% in the July-August semiconductor selloff — an index-level dated risk two days out, absent from key_risk on the top-ranked, largest-size idea. Added.

NKE DOWNGRADED 3 TO 2, ADD WITHDRAWN. This was the only continuing position where adding was still sanctioned, at 3% and conviction 3, on the strength of a 3.00 ratio. That ratio is built from a 62.00 target and a 32.00 bear case, and NKE's sole source is a finnhub price quote. No filing, no earnings release, no analyst target, no margin datapoint — a price is not evidence, and both endpoints of the arithmetic are unsupported. Every other hold in this report withdrew its add on recomputation; the one that kept its add has the weakest evidence base of the seventeen. Entry level removed, consistent with CCJ, PFE, LCII and XLE. The existing long from 40.00/38.00 stands.

BCC DOWNGRADED 3 TO 2. Its catalyst field cited "building-products demand against a 30-year Treasury yield at its highest since 2007" — the bear case for a housing-levered long, presented as its reason to exist — plus a 20-day/50-day cross. Neither of its two sources carries a building-products datapoint; one is a price quote and the other is a generic NVDA/Jackson Hole preview. Rewritten to say plainly that this is a hold-to-stop, not a thesis.

CORRELATION COUNT UNDERSTATED. The note above says HD, BCC and LCII are three expressions of one rates-and-housing bet and that the cap of three is "at its limit but not breached." KRE is a fourth: its own catalyst field names the 09-16 FOMC and a 32c hike as the driver. TLT was a fifth until today. After TLT closes the book holds four live rate-path longs against a stated cap of three — a breach, not a limit. It is not fixable by cutting one, because all four are hold-to-stop instructions on open positions and removing one deletes its stop. Recorded so the next run does not add a fifth.

THREE VALIDATOR FAILURES ARE ARTIFACTS, NOT DEFECTS. (1) The Kalshi 404s on ranks 6, 1 and 16 were transient. Re-queried live at 07:2x ET: KXFEDDECISION-26SEP-H25 returns 200 with yes_bid 31c / yes_ask 32c / last 32c, 1.74M open interest, and the H0 maintain leg at 67/68c — the 32c entry price and the 69% Robinhood cross-check in that idea are both confirmed against the exchange. It is the best-sourced idea in the report and keeps conviction 3. (2) The 4.29% CCJ and 9.37% LCII spreads that failed on liquidity are pre-market quotes on a closed market, not real trading costs; CCJ trades hundreds of millions a day. (3) DHT's earnings_date warning is a false positive — its catalyst is Frontline's 08-31 print, not DHT's own, and FRO 2026-08-31 bmo was confirmed on the fetched calendar along with DG 08-27 bmo, NVDA 08-26 amc and AVGO 09-02 amc. Every dated catalyst in this report checks out.

TWO KEPT WITH THE ARITHMETIC FLAGGED. RARE's 2.75 is computed against a 21.50 stop that its own key_risk calls "decoration" — a second CRL gaps an ultra-rare gene therapy well through it, and against a realistic 13-14 the ratio is about 1.0. The idea survives because the CMC-only CRL argument is specific, falsifiable and genuinely well sourced, and because the write-up already tells the reader to hold it as a defined full-size loss; but the 2.75 should not be read as risk control. DG's 2.88 assumes a 119.00 fill inside a 113-121 zone against a 111 stop; a gap-down fill near the bottom of that zone turns the ratio into a mirage produced by a 2-point stop. Both are entered after or around their dated events at 2%, which is the mitigation.

The composition line above is also wrong on its own count: six entries have wait=false and are acted on today (VST, DHT, NKE before this pass, RARE, the Kalshi hike contract, and the bitcoin cover), not eight. DG, AVGO and BCC are wait-for-the-print or hold instructions, and NKE has now joined the no-new-money group, making ten entries with no entry level rather than nine. Validation demoted 13 idea(s) whose numbers did not check out. 4 more carry warnings — see the validation block on each.
